phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now in this problem,
we are given that the downstream speed of a boat
is
30 kilometer
per hour.
Also, the speed of the current is five kilometer per hour.
The question is asking us to find
the
upstream speed of the boat. Now, before solving,
let us understand one simple concept.
Imagine that the river is flowing in one direction.
When the boat moves in the same direction as the river,
the current helps the boat move faster,
so both the speeds get added.
That is why downstream speed is equal to speed of boat in still water,
plus speed of current. Now, let the speed of the boat in still water be b kilometer per hour.
The downstream speed is already given as 30, and the speed of the current is five, so b plus five is equal to 30.
After solving this,
b is equal to 25 kilometers per hour.
Now, this value will help us find the upstream speed.
Why?
Because upstream means the boat is moving against the flow of the river.
So this time, the current slows the boat down. That is why upstream speed is equal to speed of boat in still water, minus speed of current.
Now, we already know the speed of the boat in still water. It is
25 kilometer per hour. So upstream speed is equal to 25 minus five.
After simplifying this, we get 20 kilometer per hour.
So the upstream speed of the boat is 20 kilometer per hour.
Hence,
the correct answer is option B.
